examples.ko: 산에서 멧돼지를 만나면 조용히 피해야 해요.
examples.en: If you meet a wild boar in the mountains, you should quietly avoid it.
A wild boar dug up the field, so the farmer is upset.

examples.ko: 멧돼지는 코로 땅을 파서 먹이를 찾아요.
examples.en: A wild boar digs the ground with its nose to find food.
I saw a baby wild boar at the zoo.
I climbed a tree to escape from the wild boar.
There is a kid who is as strong as a wild boar.

explain: 집에서 기르는 '돼지'와 달리 산에 사는 야생 돼지예요. '멧토끼', '멧새'처럼 '멧-'이 붙은 산에 사는 동물 이름도 있어요.

phrases.en: A wild boar appeared in the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산에 사는 멧돼지가 사람이 사는 곳에 갑자기 왔다는 뜻으로 뉴스에서도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a boar suddenly showing up where people live; common in news.

phrases.example: 멧돼지 고기를 먹어 본 적이 있어요?
phrases.en: Have you ever eaten wild boar meat?
phrases.nuance_ko: 집돼지 고기인 '돼지고기'와 구별해서 야생 멧돼지의 고기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Distinguishes wild boar meat from ordinary pork.

phrases.en: I saw one wild boar on the mountain path.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물은 '마리'로 세므로 수를 말할 때 이렇게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Animals are counted with 마리, so use this when giving a number.

explain_en: Unlike the farm pig, this is a wild pig living in the mountains. Other mountain animals carry the same prefix, such as 멧토끼 (wild hare) and 멧새 (bunting).

examples.en: The cat hid in the thicket.
A strange sound came from the bushes by the road.

examples.ko: 비가 온 뒤라 수풀이 더 푸르러졌어요.
examples.en: After the rain, the thicket turned even greener.
We pushed through the thicket and walked ahead.
In summer, there are lots of bugs in the thicket.
The thicket is so overgrown that I can't see the path.

explain: '숲'은 나무가 많은 넓은 곳이고, 수풀은 풀과 나무가 빽빽하게 자란 곳이에요. '수풀 속에 숨다'처럼 작은 곳을 말할 때 어울리고, 일상에서는 '숲'이 훨씬 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I pushed through the bushes and found the path.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빽빽한 풀과 나무 사이를 손으로 밀며 간다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means pushing through thick grass and trees by hand.

phrases.en: It's summer, so the thickets have grown dense.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풀과 나무가 많이 자란 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes grass and trees grown thick.

phrases.en: I took a walk in the forest on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수풀보다 넓은 곳을 말하고 일상에서 훨씬 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a larger area and is far more common than 수풀.

explain_en: 숲 is a broad area with many trees, while 수풀 is a dense growth of grass and shrubs, fitting small spots as in 수풀 속에 숨다. In daily talk 숲 is much more common.

t90.ax: The cat hid in the thicket.

en: to be very dark; to be pitch-dark

examples.ko: 방 안이 너무 컴컴해서 아무것도 안 보여요.
examples.en: The room is so dark that I can't see anything.
When evening came, the alley turned dark.
It's scary to walk alone on a dark road.

examples.ko: 정전이 돼서 집 안이 온통 컴컴해요.
examples.en: There's a power outage, so the whole house is pitch-dark.
When I turned off the light, the room turned dark.

examples.ko: 터널 안은 컴컴해도 전조등을 켜면 괜찮아요.
examples.en: The tunnel is dark, but it's fine if you turn on the headlights.

explain: '캄캄하다'와 모음만 달라서 어감이 더 크고 묵직해요. '어둡다'보다 훨씬 깜깜한 느낌이고, '어두컴컴하다'처럼 합쳐서도 써요. 변화는 '컴컴해지다'로 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: I turned on the light in the pitch-dark room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '컴컴하다'를 '-ㄴ'으로 바꿔 명사 앞에서 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -ㄴ form modifies a noun that follows.

phrases.en: After the sun set, the sky got pitch-dark.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점점 아주 어두워지는 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the change of getting very dark.

phrases.en: The underground parking lot is dim and gloomy, so it's scary.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어둡다'와 합쳐 약간 침침하고 어두운 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combined with 어둡다 for a dim, gloomy feel.

explain_en: It differs from '캄캄하다' only in vowels and sounds bigger and heavier. It feels much darker than '어둡다' and also appears in '어두컴컴하다'. Change is often said as '컴컴해지다'.

examples.ko: 여름밤에는 풀숲에서 곤충 소리가 크게 들려요.
examples.en: On summer nights, loud insect sounds come from the grass thicket.
The ball rolled into the tall grass.

examples.ko: 풀숲을 헤치고 들어가 보니 작은 연못이 있었어요.
examples.en: When I pushed through the thicket, there was a small pond.

examples.ko: 풀숲에는 모기가 많으니까 긴 바지를 입으세요.
examples.en: There are many mosquitoes in the bushes, so wear long pants.
The cat disappeared into the bushes.

examples.ko: 키 큰 풀숲 속에 새 둥지가 있었어요.
examples.en: There was a bird's nest in the tall grass.

explain: 나무가 많은 '숲'과 달리, 풀이 빽빽하게 자란 곳에 써요. '수풀'과 비슷하게 쓰는데 일상 대화에서는 '풀숲'이 더 흔히 들려요. 벌레나 작은 동물이 숨는 곳으로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The cat went into the bushes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풀숲과 비슷하지만 글이나 이야기에서도 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 풀숲 but common in writing and stories too.

phrases.en: The kids hid in the grass and played hide-and-seek.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨는 장소로 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing as a hiding place.

phrases.en: I pushed through the thicket and found the ball.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풀을 양쪽으로 밀며 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for pushing the grass aside to move through.

explain_en: Unlike '숲', which has many trees, '풀숲' is a place where grass grows thickly. It is used much like '수풀', and in everyday talk '풀숲' is the one you hear more. It often appears as a hiding place for insects and small animals.

t90.ax: The ball rolled into the tall grass.

examples.en: I bumped my knee on the corner of the desk.
The corner of the picture frame is a little broken too.

examples.ko: 가게는 골목 귀퉁이를 돌면 바로 보여요.
examples.en: The shop is right there once you turn the corner of the alley.
A corner of the wall broke off.

examples.ko: 마음 한 귀퉁이는 늘 비어 있어요.
examples.en: One corner of my heart is always empty.
Only the corner of the book is slightly folded.

explain: 물건이나 땅이 모난 곳의 끝부분을 말해요. 방 안쪽처럼 안으로 들어간 곳은 '구석'이라고 더 자주 해요. '마음 한 귀퉁이'처럼 비유로도 써요.

phrases.en: I wrote my name small on the corner of the paper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모난 물건의 끝부분을 말할 때 '물건 + 귀퉁이'로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'object + 귀퉁이' for the end of something with corners.

phrases.en: I've used the book a long time, so its corners are worn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 써서 모서리가 상했을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when a corner is worn from long use.

phrases.en: A corner of my heart still feels empty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 모양이 아니라 마음의 한 부분을 비유로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for a part of one's heart, not a physical shape.

explain_en: It refers to the tip or edge where an object or plot of land comes to a point. For an inner area like the inside of a room, '구석' is more common. It's also used figuratively, as in '마음 한 귀퉁이'.

t90.ax: A corner of the wall broke off.

examples.ko: 낚싯줄이 여러 가닥으로 꼬여서 풀기가 힘들어요.
examples.en: The fishing line is tangled in many strands and hard to untie.
A big fish bit, and the fishing line became taut.
I replaced the fishing line with a new one.
You attach a hook and bait to the end of the fishing line.
The fishing line got caught on a branch and snapped.
My father slowly reeled in the fishing line.

explain: 맞춤법에서 '낚시줄'이 아니라 사이시옷을 넣은 '낚싯줄'이 표준 표기예요. 낚싯대, 낚싯바늘처럼 낚시 도구 이름이 이렇게 이어져요.

phrases.en: I'm winding the fishing line onto the rod.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낚시를 준비하거나 마칠 때 줄을 감는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes winding the line when preparing for or finishing fishing.

phrases.en: The fishing line broke because of a big fish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어에 '끊어지다'를 붙여 줄이 끊긴 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds 'break' to the headword to describe a snapped line.

phrases.en: I cast the fishing line into the river and wait.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낚시를 시작하는 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the action of starting to fish.

explain_en: The standard spelling includes the 사이시옷, so it is '낚싯줄', not '낚시줄'. Other fishing gear names such as 낚싯대 and 낚싯바늘 follow the same pattern.

examples.en: My younger sibling broke my laptop.

examples.ko: 공공시설을 망가뜨리면 벌금을 내야 할 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you damage public facilities, you may have to pay a fine.
Be careful not to break the toy by mistake.
I didn't break it on purpose.

examples.ko: 아이가 새 우산을 또 망가뜨려서 속상해요.
examples.en: I'm upset because my child broke the new umbrella again.

examples.ko: 밤늦게 먹는 야식이 다이어트를 완전히 망가뜨려요.
examples.en: Late-night snacks completely ruin a diet.

explain: 물건이 저절로 고장 나면 '망가지다', 누군가 그렇게 만들면 '망가뜨리다'를 써요. '망가트리다'도 같은 뜻으로 쓸 수 있어요. 물건뿐 아니라 계획, 기분, 건강처럼 보이지 않는 것을 엉망으로 만들 때도 써요.

phrases.en: The child broke the toy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '망가뜨리다'와 같은 뜻이고 둘 다 써도 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '망가뜨리다'; both forms are fine.

phrases.en: Please don't break my camera.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 조심해서 다뤄 달라고 부탁할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone to handle something carefully.

phrases.example: 밤을 새우는 습관이 건강을 망가뜨릴 수 있어요.
phrases.en: The habit of staying up all night can ruin your health.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 아니라 건강처럼 보이지 않는 것을 엉망으로 만들 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for ruining intangible things like health.

explain_en: When something breaks by itself you use '망가지다', and when someone causes it you use '망가뜨리다'. '망가트리다' can be used with the same meaning. It works not only for objects but also for things like plans, mood and health that get ruined.

t90.ax: I didn't break it on purpose.

examples.en: Be sure to close the gas valve.

examples.ko: 수도 밸브가 고장 나서 물이 새요.
examples.en: The water valve is broken, so it leaks.
The man turned the valve and ran the water.
If you fix just one valve, the problem is over.
The valve for putting in air is too small.
The pressure valve opened and steam came out.

explain: '밸브'는 물이나 가스가 흐르는 양을 열고 닫아 조절하는 부품이에요. 보통 '밸브를 잠그다/열다/돌리다'로 말해요. 집에서는 '가스 밸브', '수도 밸브'처럼 쓰고 '꼭지'와 비슷하지만 밸브는 관 중간에 있는 장치도 포함해요.

phrases.en: Close the valve before you go out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흐름을 막을 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for shutting off flow.

phrases.example: 물이 안 나오면 밸브를 열어 보세요.
phrases.en: If no water comes out, try opening the valve.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흐르게 할 때는 '열다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 열다 when you want it to flow.

phrases.en: If you turn the valve to the right, it closes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손으로 돌려서 조절하는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes adjusting it by turning with your hand.

explain_en: 밸브 is the part that opens and closes to control the flow of water or gas, used with '잠그다', '열다' and '돌리다'. At home you hear '가스 밸브' and '수도 밸브'. It is close to '꼭지' (tap) but also covers devices set in the middle of a pipe.

examples.en: Grandmother is carrying vegetables on a cart.
The man pulled a cart to the market.
In the old days people carried loads by cart.
It rained, and the cart got stuck in the mud.
The kids rode on the cart and played.
I have a lot of stuff, so I need a cart.

explain: '수레'는 바퀴가 달려서 짐을 싣고 끄는 도구예요. 지금은 시장이나 공사장에서 볼 수 있어요. 마트에서 쓰는 것은 '카트', 손으로 미는 작은 것은 '손수레'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 아저씨가 짐이 가득한 수레를 밀고 가요.
phrases.en: The man is pushing a cart full of goods.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에서 끌 때는 '끌다', 뒤에서 힘을 줄 때는 '밀다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '끌다' to pull from the front and '밀다' to push from behind.

phrases.en: Grandmother loaded boxes onto a handcart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손으로 끌거나 미는 작은 수레를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A small cart that you pull or push by hand.

phrases.en: The cart wheel got caught on a stone and stopped.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수레에 달린 바퀴만 따로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to just the wheel of a cart.

explain_en: 수레 is a wheeled tool for loading and pulling goods. Today you mostly see it at markets or construction sites. The one used in a supermarket is a 카트, and a small hand-pushed one is a 손수레.

examples.en: I packed binoculars to watch birds.
Through binoculars, the mountain looks close.
Many people use binoculars at concerts.
Can you lend me your binoculars?

examples.ko: 아이가 쌍안경으로 별을 보고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: The child wants to look at stars with binoculars.
The binoculars are heavy, so my neck hurts.

explain: 두 눈으로 함께 보는 망원경이에요. '망원경'은 더 넓은 말이고, 쌍안경은 그중 두 눈으로 보는 종류예요. '쌍안경을 쓰다', '쌍안경으로 보다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I observed the stars in the night sky with binoculars.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먼 곳의 새나 별을 자세히 볼 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for looking closely at distant birds or stars.

phrases.example: 아빠가 쌍안경을 목에 걸고 산에 갔어요.
phrases.en: Dad went to the mountain with binoculars around his neck.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쌍안경을 들고 다니는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes carrying binoculars hung around the neck.
phrases.en_equiv: to hang binoculars around one's neck

phrases.en: I looked at the moon through a telescope.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쌍안경보다 넓은 말로, 한쪽 눈으로 보는 것도 포함해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word than '쌍안경', including one-eyed ones.

explain_en: It is a telescope-like device you look through with both eyes. '망원경' is the broader word, and 쌍안경 is the two-eyed kind. You say '쌍안경을 쓰다' or '쌍안경으로 보다'.

examples.en: The water bottle spilled inside the bag.

examples.ko: 컵이 쓰러지면서 우유가 엎질러져서 바닥이 젖었어요.
examples.en: The cup fell over and the milk spilled, so the floor got wet.

examples.ko: 엎질러진 우유를 닦는 동안 아이는 울지 않았어요.
examples.en: The child didn't cry while I wiped up the spilled milk.
It'd be a mess if the soup bowl spilled, so I walk slowly.

examples.ko: 물이 엎질러지는 소리에 놀라 부엌으로 달려갔어요.
examples.en: Startled by the sound of water spilling, I ran to the kitchen.

examples.ko: 그릇이 엎질러질 것 같아서 얼른 잡았어요.
examples.en: The bowl looked like it would spill, so I quickly grabbed it.

explain: '엎지르다'는 사람이 주어이고, '엎질러지다'는 물이나 그릇 같은 것이 주어로 나와요. 그래서 실수한 사람을 말하지 않고 일어난 일만 말하고 싶을 때 써요. '엎질러진 물'은 되돌릴 수 없는 일을 비유하는 말로도 써요.

phrases.en: spilled water (it's already done)
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 벌어져서 되돌릴 수 없는 일을 말할 때 써요. 후회하는 사람에게 위로하거나 이제 그만 생각하라고 할 때 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something that has already happened and can't be undone. It comes up when comforting someone who regrets it or telling them to let it go.
phrases.en_equiv: It's no use crying over spilled milk.

explain_en: With '엎지르다' a person is the subject, while with '엎질러지다' the water or container is. Use it when you want to describe what happened without naming who made the mistake. '엎질러진 물' is also used figuratively for something that can't be undone.

t90.ax: The water bottle spilled inside the bag.

examples.en: I couldn't get up even when the alarm clock rang.

examples.ko: 내일 아침 여섯 시에 자명종을 맞췄어요.
examples.en: I set the alarm clock for six o'clock tomorrow morning.
I was startled by the sound of the alarm clock.
I turned off the alarm clock and fell back asleep.

examples.ko: 할아버지 댁 자명종은 소리가 아주 커요.
examples.en: The alarm clock at Grandpa's house is very loud.
It seems the alarm clock battery has run out.

explain: 요즘은 휴대폰의 '알람'을 더 많이 쓰고, '자명종'은 알람이 달린 탁상시계를 말할 때가 많아요. '자명종을 맞추다/끄다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I set my phone alarm for seven.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요즘은 휴대폰 소리를 말할 때 '자명종'보다 '알람'을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For phone sounds, people now use this more than the headword.

phrases.en: The alarm clock rang loudly this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 날 때 쓰는 가장 기본 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic pairing for when the alarm sounds.

phrases.en: There is an alarm clock on the desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시계 물건이라는 점을 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to make clear that it is a clock as an object.

explain_en: These days people use the phone '알람' more, and '자명종' often refers to a desk clock with an alarm. Say '자명종을 맞추다/끄다'.

t90.ax: It seems the alarm clock battery has run out.

examples.ko: 문에 잠금장치가 고장 나서 열리지 않아요.
examples.en: The lock on the door is broken and it won't open.

examples.ko: 아이가 열지 못하게 서랍에 잠금장치를 달았어요.
examples.en: I put a lock on the drawer so the child can't open it.
This suitcase has a strong lock, so I feel at ease.
Be sure to check the window locks before you leave.
A bicycle without a lock is easy to get stolen.
I set up a lock on my phone.

explain: '잠금장치'는 문, 서랍, 가방, 휴대폰처럼 열리지 않게 잠그는 모든 장치를 크게 부르는 말이에요. 열쇠 있는 건 '자물쇠', 문에 달린 건 '도어락'처럼 구체적인 이름도 있어요. 휴대폰 화면에도 '잠금'을 쓰는 점이 재미있어요.

phrases.en: I unlocked it with the password.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠긴 것을 열 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when opening something that was locked.

phrases.en: The front door has a double lock.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이중'을 붙이면 잠금장치가 두 개라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 이중 means there are two locking mechanisms.

phrases.en: I always lock it when I go out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '풀다'의 반대로, 잠글 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 풀다, used when locking something.

explain_en: 잠금장치 is a broad word for any device that locks something, such as a door, drawer, bag, or phone. More specific names exist too, like 자물쇠 for a padlock with a key and 도어락 for a door lock. Koreans also use 잠금 for a phone screen lock.

t90.ax: I set up a lock on my phone.

examples.en: My mother made curtains with a sewing machine.
I could hear the sewing machine until late at night.

examples.ko: 재봉틀을 배워서 직접 옷을 고치고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to learn the sewing machine so I can fix clothes myself.
There is an old sewing machine in Grandma's room.

examples.ko: 재봉틀에 실을 끼워 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you thread the sewing machine for me?

examples.ko: 재봉틀은 바느질을 아주 빠르게 해 줘요.
examples.en: A sewing machine does stitching very fast.

explain: 손으로 하는 바느질과 달리 기계로 박는 도구예요. 일상에서는 '미싱'이라고 부르는 사람도 많아요.

phrases.en: There is an old sewing machine in my grandmother's room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '재봉틀' 대신 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word many people use instead of 재봉틀 in everyday talk.

phrases.en: My mother ran the sewing machine and made a skirt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재봉틀을 작동시켜 바느질할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation for operating a sewing machine to sew.

phrases.en: I stitched the hem of the pants with a sewing machine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손바느질이 아니라 기계로 꿰맨다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means sewing by machine rather than by hand.
phrases.en_equiv: to stitch with a sewing machine

explain_en: Unlike hand sewing, it is a machine that does the stitching. In daily life many people also call it '미싱'.
